text:
maria: dropping a follow-up from yesterday's offload sync. proposal: expose a thin per-request residency hint + a runtime admission cap per-tenant. want quick bikeshed on shapes and enforcement model before I start a spike.

kevin: do you mean a single enum or a numeric quality score? enums are easier to reason about in the short term.

maria: leaning enum for ergonomics but include optional numeric fields for advanced callers (e.g., recompute_ms_estimate, max_resident_bytes). enum candidates: resident_prefer, resident_best_effort, resident_reclaim_ok.

olivia: important: admission control. we can't let resident_prefer bypass quotas. propose per-tenant resident_quota and a rejection header if quota exhausted.

sanjay: +1. also topology matters. fetching from same-host vs cross-rack changes cost dramatically — planner needs locality input.

maria: agreed. sketch of request metadata (SDK + raw header):

```
X-Redwood-Resident: resident_prefer; recompute_ms=40; max_bytes=1MB
```

or SDK: client.call({ residency: 'resident_prefer', recompute_ms: 40 })

kevin: eviction scoring should be simple to start: base_score + topology_penalty + (recompute_ms * recompute_weight) - urgency_bonus. lower score => evict first.

olivia: also surface signals in responses: X-Redwood-Resident-Accepted: true/false and X-Redwood-Resident-Fallback: rehydrate|recompute so callers can adapt.

runtime-bot: telemetry: created metric "residency.tenant_resident_usage" -> https://console.internal/telemetry/residency/7429991234 :white_check_mark:

maria: enforcement model ideas: 1) soft admission: honor if capacity, otherwise downgrade and include fallback header. 2) strict: reject with 409 if caller asked for guaranteed residency (for Dedicated customers).

sanjay: need product input on billing — reserved vs best-effort. from infra side we can implement both semantics.

kevin: implementation constraints: marking pages resident needs O(1) hot path. can't walk big lists per request. use a per-allocation residency flag + increment resident_count per-tenant. eviction daemon reads counts.

maria: timeline: spike to prototype header parsing + simple scoring in the evictor next week. I'll include topology-aware cost model stub and a tenant quota check.

olivia: telemetry request: per-urgency resident_hit_rate and rehydrate_latency_by_topology. that'll help tune defaults.

maria: good. I'll add SDK validation (warn on recompute_ms > 10s) and server-side caps to avoid abuse.

kevin: corner case: batched requests where some items are resident_prefer and others not. how do we aggregate? treat batch as max urgency among items? or per-entry residency tracking?

maria: prefer per-entry tracking but fall back to batch-level behavior if SDK doesn't provide per-item hints. will document tradeoffs.

olivia: can you add a short section in the RFC about cross-tenant fairness (tenant_quota + eviction_credit system) so PM has something to review?

maria: yep. action: I'll open an RFC with header shapes, admission rules, eviction scoring draft, and a tiny benchmark comparing local rehydrate vs recompute for two common transformer sizes. tagging @olivia @kevin @sanjay for review.

runtime-bot: deploy: residency-hook v0.4 staged at 7429991248

kevin: small follow-up: include a fallback enum in SDK so app code can switch to a cheap-mode if fallback=recompute.

maria: done. PR incoming. thanks all!
